newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower in anticipated correction.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower in anticipated correction.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled weaker but off the day's lows, after today's consumption data and new sales reports failed to maintain prices at recent highs, market sources said.
Analysts had anticipated lower prices in the face of of abundant world supplies, weak demand, and the gap between U.S. and foreign prices.

A strong consumption figure may have supported December around 73.00, today's highs. But the U.S. Census Bureau put average daily use at 40,175 bales in September, barely changed from 40,184 bales in August.
Analysts viewed the number as weak because demand is historically higher in September.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture's export and sales report also failed to inspire prices. The USDA put sales for the week ended Oct 17 at 234,200 480-lb bales, below market expectations.
December ended 0.88 lower at 72.20, having ranged from 73.00 to 71.90. The deferred months closed 0.83 to 0.25 lower.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots. Dealers noted aggressive trade selling and speculative selling below 72.50 in December.
